questions.enonce_markdown: Solve for $x$ in the equation $4^x + 2^{2+x} = 12$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Express everything with base $2$: $4^x = (2^2)^x = (2^x)^2$ and $2^{2+x} = 2^2\cdot 2^x = 4\cdot 2^x$. Let $u = 2^x$, with $u > 0$:

$$u^2 + 4u = 12 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u^2 + 4u - 12 = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (u + 6)(u - 2) = 0.$$

So $u = -6$ or $u = 2$. Since $2^x > 0$ for every real $x$, $u = -6$ is rejected. Hence $2^x = 2$:

$$\boxed{x = 1}$$

Check: $4^1 + 2^{3} = 4 + 8 = 12$.

questions.enonce_markdown: The determinant of a matrix $M$ is $45$, where $M = \begin{pmatrix} \alpha & 3 & 5 \\ 4 & \alpha - 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. Show that $\alpha = 2$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Expand $\det M$ along the first row:

$$\det M = \alpha\bigl[(\alpha - 1)(0) - 6(4)\bigr] - 3\bigl[4(0) - 6(1)\bigr] + 5\bigl[4(4) - (\alpha - 1)(1)\bigr]$$

$$= -24\alpha + 18 + 5(17 - \alpha) = -24\alpha + 18 + 85 - 5\alpha = 103 - 29\alpha.$$

Given $\det M = 45$:

$$103 - 29\alpha = 45 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 29\alpha = 58 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \alpha = 2. \qquad \blacksquare$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
With $M = \begin{pmatrix} \alpha & 3 & 5 \\ 4 & \alpha - 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\alpha = 2$, find $M^{-1}$, the inverse of the matrix $M$. Hence, solve the system of equations

$$
2x + 3y + 5z = 30
$$

$$
4x + y + 6z = 27
$$

$$
x + 4y \phantom{+ 5z} = 45
$$

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $\alpha = 2$:

$$M = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 4 & 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \det M = 45.$$

**Cofactors** $C_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}\times(\text{minor})$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
C_{11} &= 1\cdot 0 - 6\cdot 4 = -24, & C_{12} &= -(4\cdot 0 - 6\cdot 1) = 6, & C_{13} &= 4\cdot 4 - 1\cdot 1 = 15,\\
C_{21} &= -(3\cdot 0 - 5\cdot 4) = 20, & C_{22} &= 2\cdot 0 - 5\cdot 1 = -5, & C_{23} &= -(2\cdot 4 - 3\cdot 1) = -5,\\
C_{31} &= 3\cdot 6 - 5\cdot 1 = 13, & C_{32} &= -(2\cdot 6 - 5\cdot 4) = 8, & C_{33} &= 2\cdot 1 - 3\cdot 4 = -10.
\end{aligned}
$$

The adjugate is the transpose of the cofactor matrix, and $M^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{\det M}\operatorname{adj}M$:

$$\boxed{M^{-1} = \frac{1}{45}\begin{pmatrix} -24 & 20 & 13 \\ 6 & -5 & 8 \\ 15 & -5 & -10 \end{pmatrix}}$$

Check: first row of $M$ times first column of the adjugate: $2(-24) + 3(6) + 5(15) = -48 + 18 + 75 = 45$, giving $1$ on the diagonal; first row of $M$ times second column: $2(20) + 3(-5) + 5(-5) = 40 - 15 - 25 = 0$.

**Solving the system.** The system is $M\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 30 \\ 27 \\ 45 \end{pmatrix}$, so

$$\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = M^{-1}\begin{pmatrix} 30 \\ 27 \\ 45 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{45}\begin{pmatrix} -24(30) + 20(27) + 13(45) \\ 6(30) - 5(27) + 8(45) \\ 15(30) - 5(27) - 10(45) \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{45}\begin{pmatrix} -720 + 540 + 585 \\ 180 - 135 + 360 \\ 450 - 135 - 450 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{45}\begin{pmatrix} 405 \\ 405 \\ -135 \end{pmatrix}.$$

$$\boxed{x = 9, \qquad y = 9, \qquad z = -3}$$

Check in the original equations: $2(9) + 3(9) + 5(-3) = 18 + 27 - 15 = 30$; $4(9) + 9 + 6(-3) = 36 + 9 - 18 = 27$; $9 + 4(9) = 45$.
